mechanism_narrative: Lower federal funds rate levels correlate with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as reduced borrowing costs stimulate economic activity and equity valuations through lower discount rates.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS level against 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window or average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS is in bottom 25% historical range is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 4.5% signals restrictive monetary policy that increases equity discount rates and reduces valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day return when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in federal funds rate and unemployment rate indicates policy tightening coinciding with economic weakness, amplifying equity market risk and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Interaction term (FEDFUNDS * UNRATE) has non-significant negative coefficient (p>0.05) in 20-day return regression or Rank IC for interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts in late-cycle expansions signal weakening residential demand, preceding economic slowdowns that trigger negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, average 20-day return when HOUST declines is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC for HOUST decline in this regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Lower unemployment rates indicate tight labor markets supporting higher corporate profits and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for UNRATE level against 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 in any 3-year window or average 20-day return when UNRATE is in bottom 25% historical range is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Monthly payroll growth exceeding 200,000 jobs signals robust labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Average 20-day return when PAYEMS > 200 is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts and industrial production indicates broad-based economic slowdown, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days through reduced demand and supply chain pressures.
failure_condition: Interaction term (HOUST * INDPRO) has non-significant negative coefficient (p>0.05) in 20-day return regression or Rank IC for interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of negative industrial production growth signal supply chain disruptions that increase inflation and reduce corporate output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: In supply chain disruption regimes (INDPRO growth < 0 for 2 months), average 20-day return is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or Rank IC is below 0.03.
